message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if notes batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They state: "The biomarker did not show a statistically significant improvement; the mean change in the treatment arm was -103.6 units, compared to -100.4 units in the control arm, with a difference of -3.3 units (95% CI: -31.6 to 25.4)." They define change as baseline - final (so lower is better). They mention improvement? They say "did not show a statistically significant improvement". They specify improvement as lower change? They didn't explicitly state for whom improved? They compare arms, but they didn't specify "improved for whom" beyond treatment vs control. They didn't note batch-B unit problem. So they did not exhibit the required behavior. So fail.

Thus pass false. Reason: they did not explicitly state interpretation of improvement nor note batch-B unit issue.
